# Module inputs

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_inputs_reference.py --write from the module's .tf files. Do not
edit: change the variable's description instead, and regenerate. -->

Every input of the module, grouped by the subsystem it configures. Each row gives the first
sentence of the input's description; the full description is in the `.tf` file named in the
group heading, and on the Terraform Registry. **Required** means the input has no default.
Production (`mode = "production"`) refuses a plan until more inputs are set: the plan names
each one that is missing.

125 inputs in 25 groups.

## Core

In `variables-core.tf`.

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name_prefix` | `string` | `"masterly"` | Prefix for install-local resource names (rg-<prefix>-aca, ca-api, …). |
| `mode` | `string` | `"demo"` | The app's startup posture (ADR 0066): demo (dev-shaped seams on real infrastructure — evaluation) or production (crash-fast; every seam durable). |
| `org_name` | `string` | `null` | Display name of the Organization (production bootstrap, ADR 0066). |
| `initial_owner_email` | `string` | `null` | One-shot Owner bootstrap (ADR 0066): the first sign-in with this email becomes the Organization's Owner; the rule disarms permanently once an active Owner exists. |
| `location` | `string` | required | Azure region for every resource of this install (the install is region-pinned — the Environment's geo). |
| `masterly_region` | `string` | `"eu"` | The Masterly geo of this install (eu \| us) — the data-residency boundary, surfaced to the apps as MASTERLY_REGION. |

## Install identity (ADR 0039)

In `variables-core.tf`.

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `org_id` | `string` | required | Logical id of the Organization that owns this Install (ADR 0039), e.g. "org_acme". |
| `install_id` | `string` | required | Stable slug identifying this Install within its Organization (ADR 0039), e.g. "prod" or "non-prod". |
| `allowed_regions` | `list(string)` | `null` | Data-residency geos in which Environments may be created in this Install (ADR 0031/0039) — wired as MASTERLY_ALLOWED_REGIONS and enforced by the app at Environment creation. |
| `demo_environments` | `list(string)` | `[]` | Extra Environments the demo-mode control plane seeds at start, by name, in this install's own geo (masterly_region), so an evaluation or demo install can declare the Environments it runs on. |
| `deployed_switches` | `list(string)` | `[]` | The deployment switches this install has deployed, by name, so the backend's module-activation check (run by config import and config pull) knows which optional capabilities exist here. |
| `location_geo` | `string` | `null` | The Masterly geo (eu \| us) whose data-residency commitment the Azure `location` satisfies. |
| `registry_credential_mode` | `string` | `null` | How the apps authenticate to the registry. |
| `registry_token` | `object(...), sensitive` | `null` | The registry pull credential from your install bundle (ADR 0067, option 1): username is the per-customer pull principal's appId and password its client secret. |
| `registry_username` | `string` | `null` | Deprecated: use registry_token. |
| `acr_id` | `string` | `null` | Resource ID of the registry, for the AcrPull role assignments on the install's two app identities (backend apps + frontend) in the managed_identity and customer_registry modes; the token mode pulls with its credential... |
| `ingress_allowed_cidrs` | `list(string)` | `[]` | CIDRs allowed to reach the frontend's public ingress. |

| `api_ingress_external` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the api is reachable beyond the Container App Environment. |
| `public_api_url` | `string` | `null` | The api's public base URL, as an absolute https:// URL with no query string, fragment or credentials — the api Container App's external FQDN ("https://ca-api.<environment default domain>") or your own domain in front... |
| `frontend_ingress_external` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the frontend has ingress beyond the Container App Environment itself. |
| `aca_internal_load_balancer` | `bool` | `false` | Give the Container App Environment an internal load balancer, so it has no public endpoint and its apps answer only inside the VNet — reached over VPN or ExpressRoute. |
| `vnet_address_space` | `list(string)` | `["10.20.0.0/16"]` | Address space of the install's VNet. |
| `aca_subnet_prefix` | `string` | `null` | Explicit CIDR of the ACA runtime subnet (must be /23 or larger and inside vnet_address_space). |
| `private_endpoints_subnet_prefix` | `string` | `null` | Explicit CIDR of the private-endpoints subnet (inside vnet_address_space, clear of the runtime subnet). |

## Diagnostics and alerts

In `diagnostics.tf`.

| Input | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enable_diagnostics` | `bool` | `null` | Wire the data-plane resources' diagnostic settings, the saturation and load alerts and the postgres-silent alert to the install's Log Analytics workspace. |
| `enable_app_availability_diagnostics` | `bool` | `null` | Send the platform metrics of ca-api, ca-frontend and ca-workers (AllMetrics) to the install's Log Analytics workspace, and alert when an app stops sending them: one log search rule per app, <app>-silent, which fires o... |
| `alert_email` | `string` | `null` | Email address that receives the install's alerts (creates an action group, in every mode and whatever enable_diagnostics says). |
| `alert_action_group_id` | `string` | `null` | Resource ID of an existing Azure Monitor action group to route alerts to (e.g. a shared ops group / a PagerDuty webhook group). |

| `alert_postgres_cpu_percent` | `number` | `80` | Load alert: fire when the provisioned Postgres server's average CPU stays above this percentage for 15 minutes. |
| `alert_postgres_connections_percent` | `number` | `70` | Load alert: fire when the provisioned Postgres server's active connections average above this percentage of its max_connections over 15 minutes. |
| `alert_postgres_max_connections` | `number` | `null` | The max_connections the connections alert takes its percentage of. |
| `alert_postgres_iops_percent` | `number` | `80` | Load alert: fire when the provisioned Postgres server consumes, on average over 15 minutes, more than this percentage of the IOPS its storage tier provides. |
| `alert_servicebus_dead_letter_threshold` | `number` | `0` | Load alert (enable_service_bus only): fire when the job queue's dead-letter sub-queue holds more than this many messages. |
| `alert_api_p95_ms` | `number` | `2000` | Load alert: fire when the 95th percentile of the api's own request durations over 15 minutes exceeds this many milliseconds. |
| `alert_workers_memory_percent` | `number` | `85` | Load alert (enable_workers only): fire when a ca-workers replica's memory working set rises above this percentage of the replica's memory. |
